evals.name: optimize-blog-draft
evals.prompt: I've got a draft blog post at C:/tmp/seo-onpage-evals/agentic-workflows-draft.md targeting the keyword "agentic ai workflows". Before I publish it, can you go over the on-page side and tell me what needs fixing? I want the actual replacement title and meta description written out, not just told they're wrong.
evals.expected_output: A measured on-page report on the draft: title and meta description flagged against 50-60 and 105-155 char thresholds with written replacements, heading hierarchy problems named, evidence/citation gaps identified, and judgment calls (does the opening answer the query) surfaced rather than guessed.
assertions: Writes out a concrete replacement SEO title (not just says the current one is too long)
The proposed title is between 50 and 60 characters
Writes out a concrete replacement meta description
The proposed meta description is between 105 and 155 characters
Identifies the skipped heading level (an H2 is followed by an H4)
Flags that the draft contains no outbound citations or named sources
Flags the non-descriptive anchor text 'Click here'
Flags the image for missing alt text or its camera-style filename (IMG_4471)
Flags the URL slug for using underscores, uppercase, or a date path
Treats 'does the opening actually answer the query' as a judgment call with evidence shown, rather than silently asserting a pass

evals.name: audit-live-page
evals.prompt: Can you do an on-page audit of https://example.com/ ? They're a renaissance faire, main query is "renaissance faire near me". I need something I can actually send them - what's broken, in priority order.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized audit with a one-line diagnosis, roughly three ranked fixes each with measured evidence, a 'what is fine' section, and an explicit statement that Search Console is not connected. Not a list of forty findings.
assertions: States explicitly that Google Search Console data is not available/connected
Contains a single-sentence diagnosis naming what is actually wrong, not a generic summary
Presents five or fewer top-priority fixes rather than an unranked list of every issue
Includes a section stating what is already fine / working
Cites at least one directly measured number (LCP seconds, image byte count, orphan page count, or character count)
Does not state any traffic, click, impression or CTR figure as fact
Identifies the title tag problem (no 'renaissance faire' variant in the title, or title/H1 disagreement)
Ranks fixes by impact rather than listing them in checklist order

evals.name: diagnose-low-ctr
evals.prompt: one of my client's service pages is sitting on page 2 for its main keyword and getting basically no clicks even though it shows up in search a fair bit. the page is https://moz.com/learn/seo/meta-description and the keyword is "meta description". what would you actually change on the page? and is there stuff the top results cover that this page doesn't?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses this as a metadata/CTR problem before a content problem, measures the page's title/meta against thresholds, runs a term-gap analysis against the live top 10 splitting body vs heading terms, and is honest that impressions/CTR figures cannot be confirmed without Search Console.
assertions: Correctly works out whether this is a POSITION problem or a CTR problem rather than assuming CTR - a page on page 2 earns ~0.5-1.5% CTR no matter how good the snippet is
Measures the page's actual current title and/or meta description rather than speaking generically
Performs a real comparison against the pages currently ranking for the query
Separates missing heading/section topics from missing body concepts, or otherwise distinguishes structural gaps from prose gaps
States that the impressions/CTR claim cannot be verified without Search Console access
Does not prescribe a keyword density or a 'use this term N times' target
Proposes concrete rewritten metadata rather than only describing what to change
